transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have our first case-management conference in three weeks, and I need to approve our litigation plan before we go any further. The current draft preserves both claims 7 and 12, pursues broad technical discovery, and allows source-code production under the opposing party's proposed protective order. Before I sign off on this plan, I need to hear from both of you: patent litigation counsel, is there anything about our claim strategy, validity, or infringement positions that should change what's in this draft? And to our technology liaison, are there any technical realities, source-code concerns, or product architecture issues that should alter our discovery scope or protective order approach? I'd rather adjust now than scramble before the conference.

Thank you both. This is exactly why we do this review before I approve. Let me summarize what needs to change in the draft plan based on what you've told me.

First, Thomas — you've identified a 2016 published software implementation that anticipates every limitation of claim 7, giving us a strong invalidity position on that claim, while claim 12 remains intact with no equivalent prior art found. That's significant. It means we need to revise the plan to reflect an invalidity defense on claim 7, and we should consider whether continuing to actively pursue or preserve claim 7 in its current posture still makes strategic sense, or whether we should shift our emphasis toward claim 12 as the primary infringement claim while asserting invalidity against claim 7 defensively.

Second, Nadia — the opposing party's proposed protective order is inadequate because it allows two named employees to access our source code, but our board-approved security policy requires that source-code access be limited to outside counsel and independent experts who have signed enhanced source-code acknowledgments. That means the plan must be revised to require those enhanced restrictions before any source-code production occurs.

So the revisions I'm directing before I will approve this plan are: (1) update the claim strategy to reflect the invalidity position on claim 7 based on the 2016 prior art, with claim 12 as the primary surviving claim; (2) revise the protective order approach to require access limited to outside counsel and independent experts with enhanced source-code acknowledgments, replacing the opposing party's proposed terms; and (3) maintain the broad technical discovery scope, since we'll need it both to support our infringement position on claim 12 and to develop the invalidity defense on claim 7.

Thomas, can you circulate the revised claim analysis by end of this week? Nadia, please coordinate with Thomas to draft the proposed protective order modifications and confirm they align with the board-approved security policy. I want the revised plan on my desk no later than ten days before the case-management conference so I have time to review and approve. Are there any obstacles to that timeline from either of you?
